description: Basks all day, crusted and cracked open on the light beneath, then gets up breathing fire it never learned.
lore: What fell was small: a damp thing the length of a hand, bark-coloured, living under wet wood, no danger to anything and in none itself. What basks on the black rock now stands several times that — hide gone to crust, the crust split along its seams on a steady light, and when the mouth opens, fire comes out. A great many of the dead once put a log on a fire and watched a little creature run out of the flame; every one of them drew the obvious conclusion, and not one went back and checked. When the animal's own account of itself wore thin, their story is what was left holding the shape.

It spends the day flat on the warm stone, doing just what the story says it should, then gets up and walks a round nothing accounts for and bites whatever is standing in it — and the fire makes the bite the smaller half of the problem. [[characters/cfe826c1|Jehanne]] walks out once a season to look at it. She keeps a rite she stopped believing because people need the fire either way, and she says this creature is her whole argument, standing up and warm.

The coal it finally comes down to [[items/red_seam_pyre_stone|does not cool]]. The black rock runs on toward the cave, warmer the whole way, and the creature walks to the edge of that ground and turns back, every time.
